div.h1: Preparing for Your Online TRE™ Session
div.p: Everything to set up before we meet online — your space, your camera, your kit and your safety. Please read this through before your first session.

div.h2: Your Setup Is Part of the Practice

div.p: In an online session, everything your facilitator can offer you comes through the camera — watching how your body moves, how your tremors travel, and when it’s time to pause. A few minutes of preparation lets us give you the same quality of attention you would receive in the room.

Please make sure you have enough space to place your device far enough away that we can see your whole body — standing upright during the preparation exercises, and lying on your mat during the TRE™ practice itself.

The one thing that matters most: we must be able to see you head to toe, both standing and on the mat. If we can only see part of you, we cannot guide you safely — so please test your camera before the session starts.
Two views to check before every session — standing, and on the mat.

svg.aria-label: Diagram showing a device placed about two to two and a half metres away, angled so a standing person is visible from head to feet.

div.p: Step back until your feet and the top of your head are both inside the frame with a little room to spare. Landscape orientation, camera at roughly hip height.

svg.aria-label: Diagram showing a device placed to the side of a yoga mat, angled so the whole mat and a person lying in butterfly position are visible.
svg.text: Place the device to the side of the mat —
not at your head or feet

div.h3: 2. On the mat — the tremoring practice
div.p: Set the device to the side of your mat so the full length of your body stays in shot, including your knees in the butterfly position.

li.span: Use landscape orientation and prop the device so it cannot slide or fall.
A larger screen helps — you need to follow the exercises being demonstrated.
Join a few minutes early and check your own video preview before we start.
Leave room to step forward and back without walking out of frame.

div.p: Have all of this ready and within reach before the session begins.
Somewhere comfortable and non-slip to lie down for the tremoring practice.
Laptop, tablet or phone — the bigger the screen the better, so you can clearly see the exercises being shown.
Essential in group classes, as you’ll be far from the device. In private sessions we can try without — but please have a pair ready to connect.
A stable connection throughout. If you can, sit close to your router or use a wired connection.
For support under your knees or head, and to stay warm as your body settles afterwards.
Light the room well and face the light where possible. If you are backlit or in shadow, we can’t see your movement.
Stretchy and comfortable enough for the butterfly position. Dark clothing hides your tremors from the camera, so please avoid black.
Keep a glass or bottle beside your mat so you don’t have to leave the frame.
Let the household know, silence notifications, and close the door so you can let go completely.
Please ask someone you trust to be in the same house or apartment as you — or right next door — for the duration of the session, and give us their name and phone number on your consent form.
This is rarely needed. It simply means that if you would benefit from someone physically present, we can reach them straight away. Having their details on the form is the important part.
Our online sessions and group classes run on Zoom. Only authenticated users can join, and only through the Zoom application — so please set this up in advance rather than on the day.

ol.li: Download the Zoom client app for your desktop or mobile device from zoom.us/download.
Create or sign in to a Zoom account using the same email address you registered with.
Test your camera and microphone inside the app before the session day.
Join through the app, not the browser — joining from a browser or while signed out may block you from the session.
If Zoom is new to you, allow ten extra minutes the first time. There are plenty of short walkthroughs online, and we’re happy to help you test in advance.
Roll out your mat and clear the space around it.
Set your device in place and check the two camera views above — standing, and lying down.
Turn on the lights; close curtains if you are backlit.
Put cushions, a blanket and water beside your mat.
Charge or plug in your device, and connect your headphones.
Confirm your support person knows the session is happening.
Open Zoom, sign in, and join a few minutes early.

div.p: If anything about your setup is unclear — the space, the camera, the kit — please ask before your session rather than on the day. We’re glad to help you get it right.
